verdict.summary: Clio does not review Manage apps that are not listed in its App Directory. Once you have a paid or developer Clio account, you can create an app and connect to it straight away. Clio only reviews apps for an App Directory listing, which involves a security questionnaire, a recorded demo and a listing form. The main costs are the account requirement (no sandbox, paid account or approved developer account) and a fixed rate limit of 50 requests per minute at peak.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to create the app and connect. Several days of work to prepare an App Directory listing (policies, security questionnaire, demo).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30 min if you already have a paid or trial Clio Manage account
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account or other firms authorizing an unlisted app. Clio publishes no end-to-end timeline for an App Directory listing.

steps.title: Get a Clio Manage account in your region
steps.detail: Start a free 7-day Clio Manage trial in the region you are targeting (US is app.clio.com), or use an existing paid account. Clio has no sandbox, so this account is your test environment. Creating an app and getting its key and secret requires a paid account (not EasyStart) or an approved developer account.
gotchas: The EasyStart tier cannot create apps
Each region needs its own account and its own app

steps.title: Apply to convert the trial to a developer account
steps.detail: If you are not using a paid account, apply for a free developer account before the 7-day trial ends. Clio reviews the application and, if you are eligible, converts the trial account.
gotchas: Clio does not publish a review time. Apply early so you don't lose access.

steps.title: Sign in to the Clio Manage developer portal
steps.detail: Go to developers.clio.com and sign in with your Clio Manage account. This is not the Clio Platform portal (developers.api.clio.com), which uses separate accounts and separate apps.
gotchas: If you also integrate with Clio Platform, you need a second app in that portal

steps.title: Create the developer application
steps.detail: Create a new app. Fill in Name and Website URL, add the redirect URI, and accept the Developer Terms of Service. Description, icon and support URL are optional. The redirect_uri in every authorize request must match one of the URIs listed on the app.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Paste the callback URL exactly as Composio shows it. Clio's Platform docs require an exact match on protocol, domain and path, and the Manage docs require the URI to match one of the app's URIs.
Endpoints shown are for the US region

steps.title: Choose the minimum access permissions
steps.detail: Make a list of the resources your agent actually uses, and choose read-only or read/write for each one in the app's access permissions. Request as little as possible. Users see this list when they authorize. Clio Payments API access also needs the user to accept the clio_payments scope.
gotchas: You can change permissions later, but users who already authorized keep their old grants until they re-authorize

steps.title: Optionally set a deauthorization callback
steps.detail: If you want to be notified when a user revokes access, enter a Deauthorization callback URL in the app settings. Clio sends a POST request to that URL when a token is deauthorized.

steps.title: Add the app key and secret to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the App Key (client_id) and App Secret from the app page into a custom OAuth auth config in Composio, using Clio's authorize and token URLs. The App ID is a different value from the App Key and differs by region. Use the App Key as the client_id.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio has no catalog toolkit for Clio, so there is no managed app to fall back on

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, approve the app in Clio, and confirm that the token exchange succeeds and an API call returns data. The authorization code expires 10 minutes after approval. The token request must be a form-encoded POST that includes client_id, client_secret, grant_type, code and redirect_uri.
gotchas: Access tokens expire after 30 days, so the refresh flow must work
A bad client_id may only send you to a sign-in page instead of showing a clear OAuth error
PKCE does not appear in Clio's Manage docs

steps.title: Let users at other firms connect without a listing
steps.detail: Clio does not review apps that are not listed in the App Directory. Users at other firms connect through the same OAuth flow. Expect a firm admin to be involved in granting access. Each access token is limited to 50 requests per minute at peak, and Clio does not raise this limit.
gotchas: Handle HTTP 429 responses by waiting for the time in the Retry-After header
No install cap is documented for unlisted apps. Confirm with Clio if you expect wide distribution.

steps.title: Publish policies and harden security
steps.detail: Draft and publish a Terms of Service, Security Policy and Privacy Policy. Serve the app over HTTPS with strong TLS and keep secrets out of public repositories. Check the app against the red flags in Clio's security guidelines.

steps.title: Request and complete the security questionnaire
steps.detail: Email api.partnerships@clio.com to request the security and compliance questionnaire, then fill it in and return it. Clio's Application Security and Compliance team reviews your answers and either approves them or asks for changes.

steps.title: Wait for security approval
steps.detail: Clio reviews the questionnaire and may ask for changes. These docs give no end-to-end timeline for the listing process.

steps.title: Send a pre-recorded demo
steps.detail: Once security is approved, record a walkthrough of your app and its Clio integration and email it to api.partnerships@clio.com. Clio uses the demo to judge how the app serves customer needs.

steps.title: Complete the App Directory listing and Add to Clio
steps.detail: Fill in the App Directory listing form. Clio drafts the listing for you to review before it is published. Have onboarding content and supported browser versions ready, and show at least 99% uptime over 30 days. After you are listed, you can implement the 'Add to Clio' flow from the Clio Manage integrations page.

requirements.item: Paid Clio Manage account (not EasyStart) or approved developer account
requirements.detail: Needed to create apps and get the app key and secret. Clio has no sandbox.

requirements.item: App name, website URL, redirect URI and acceptance of the Developer Terms of Service
requirements.detail: Required fields on the Manage app form.

requirements.item: A separate account and app for each region
requirements.detail: US, EU, CA and AU each need their own Clio account and Developer Application. App IDs differ by region.
Access tokens last 30 days. Refresh tokens do not expire.

requirements.item: Published Terms of Service, Security Policy and Privacy Policy; HTTPS with strong TLS
requirements.detail: Required by Clio's security and data guidelines.

requirements.item: Approved security questionnaire, pre-recorded demo, listing form
requirements.detail: The App Directory launch process, run through api.partnerships@clio.com.

requirements.item: At least 99% uptime over 30 days, onboarding content, supported browser versions
requirements.detail: Listing criteria in Clio's App Developer Guide.

scopes.effect: Chosen on the app in the developer portal and shown to users at consent. Changing them requires existing users to re-authorize. Clio publishes no sensitive or restricted tiers for these permissions.
The authenticating user must accept this scope before the app can use the Clio Payments API.

blockers.symptom: You cannot create an app or see a key and secret
blockers.cause: The account is on EasyStart, or is an expired trial that was never converted to a developer account.
blockers.fix: Use a paid Clio plan, or apply for a free developer account before the 7-day trial ends.

blockers.symptom: The authorize step fails or the callback is rejected
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri does not match a redirect URI listed on the app.
blockers.fix: Paste Composio's callback URL into the app's redirect URIs exactly as shown.

blockers.cause: The limit is 50 requests per minute per access token at peak, and Clio grants no custom increases.
blockers.fix: Respect the Retry-After header, then batch requests or spread them over time.

blockers.symptom: New permissions are missing for existing users
blockers.cause: Users who already authorized keep their original grants.
blockers.fix: Prompt those users to re-authorize the app.

blockers.symptom: Clio declines the directory listing or blocks API access
blockers.cause: The app shows security red flags or is missing required policies.
blockers.fix: Follow Clio's security and data guidelines before you submit.

blockers.symptom: Users in the EU, CA or AU cannot connect
blockers.cause: Apps are specific to one region.
blockers.fix: Create a Clio account and an app in each region, each with its own auth config.

composio.note: These findings show no Composio toolkit or managed OAuth app for Clio, so you need to register your own Clio Manage app and set up a custom OAuth auth config (authorize URL https://app.clio.com/oauth/authorize, token URL https://app.clio.com/oauth/token for the US region). Paste Composio's callback URL into the app's redirect URIs. Access permissions are set on the Clio app rather than through a scope string. Check the Composio dashboard in case Clio support has been added since this research.

evidence.claim: The Clio Manage developer portal at developers.clio.com is where Clio Manage OAuth applications get created, separate from the Clio Platform portal.
evidence.quote: The Clio Manage developer portal is located at https://developers.clio.com and is the location for creating your Clio Manage OAuth Applications.

evidence.claim: Each Manage app has an App ID distinct from the App Key, and IDs differ by region, so US and EU apps have different IDs.
evidence.quote: Application IDs are different for each region of Clio Manage your app is available in.

evidence.claim: An app that runs in several Clio regions needs a Clio account and a separate Developer Application in each region.
evidence.quote: If your app operates in multiple Clio regions, you will need a Clio account and Developer Application in each region.

evidence.claim: Manage scopes are labelled access permissions in Clio's docs; the developer picks them on app creation, choosing read-only or read/write per resource, and users see the list when authorizing.
evidence.quote: You can choose between read-only and read/write access for each permission, depending on your needs.

evidence.claim: Clio advises requesting the smallest permission set that still lets the app work.
evidence.quote: You should choose the smallest set necessary for your application to function properly

evidence.claim: Permissions can be edited at any time, but users already authorized keep their old grants and must re-authorize to receive new ones.
evidence.quote: If you change permissions, you'll need to prompt your users to reauthorize your application

evidence.claim: Clio Payments access needs the authenticating user to accept a separate clio_payments scope during authorization.
evidence.quote: Access to Clio Payments API will require the authenticating user to accept the clio_payments scope

evidence.claim: An authorization code is valid for 10 minutes after the user approves, and it is exchanged at app.clio.com/oauth/token.
evidence.quote: The code is valid for 10 minutes.

evidence.claim: The token exchange must be a form-encoded POST that includes client credentials, the grant type, the code and the redirect_uri.
evidence.quote: Note that this request must specify the application/x-www-form-urlencoded content-type

evidence.claim: Access tokens expire after 30 days, so a refresh flow is needed; refresh tokens do not expire.
evidence.quote: Access token has expired (tokens last 30 days)

evidence.claim: The Manage authorization docs list only client_id, client_secret and redirect_uri for the exchange and show no PKCE parameter, so PKCE does not appear to be documented for Manage.
Signing into the Manage developer portal uses a Clio Manage account, while the Clio Platform developer portal is a separate account.
evidence.quote: The Clio Manage developer portal uses Manage accounts to sign in and make changes to your OAuth applications.

evidence.claim: Clio Platform app redirect URIs must match exactly, including protocol, domain and path.
evidence.quote: These must be exact matches, including protocol (http/https), domain, and path.

evidence.claim: A deauthorization callback URL can be set in Manage app settings, and Clio sends a POST to it when a token is deauthorized.
evidence.quote: Clio will make a `POST` request to the specified URL.

evidence.claim: The Manage API default is 50 requests per minute during peak hours, higher off-peak, and Clio does not offer custom rate-limit increases for apps.
evidence.quote: We do not support custom rate limit increases for applications at this time.

evidence.claim: Rate limits apply per access token, and a 429 with Retry-After is returned once the limit is exceeded.
evidence.quote: Requests to API v4 are rate-limited by access token.

evidence.claim: Launch in the Clio App Directory starts with a security and compliance questionnaire: the developer emails the API Partnerships team to request it, and Clio's Application Security and Compliance team reviews the answers and approves or asks for changes.
evidence.quote: To request a security questionnaire, email our API Partnerships team at api.partnerships@clio.com

evidence.claim: After security approval, the Manage path requires a pre-recorded demo emailed to the API Partnerships team, followed by an App Directory listing form that Clio drafts for review before publishing.
evidence.quote: send an email to our API Partnerships team (api.partnerships@clio.com) with a pre-recorded demo

evidence.claim: Directory listing requires passing security review, onboarding content, supported browser versions for web apps, and 99% uptime over a 30-day rolling window.
evidence.quote: Demonstrate at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis for core functionality

evidence.claim: Clio's security guidelines require HTTPS with strong TLS, secrets kept out of public repos, and published Terms of Service, Security Policy and Privacy Policy.
evidence.quote: Maintain a publicly visible Terms of Service, Security Policy, and Privacy Policy.

evidence.claim: Clio may decline a directory listing or block API access for an app that shows the red flags listed in its security guidelines.
evidence.quote: Below are a few red flags that can lead Clio to decline listing an app on the Clio App Directory and/or block Clio Public API access for the App

evidence.claim: A probe of developers.clio.com redirected to a Clio account sign-in page, so the portal sits behind a login wall.
evidence.quote: Sign in to Clio Developer Portal US Email Next: Password

evidence.claim: The demo is a pre-recorded walkthrough of the app and integration, where Clio checks how the app serves customer needs.
evidence.quote: Clio will conduct a review through a pre-recorded demonstration of your app and integration.

evidence.claim: The Add to Clio flow starts from Clio Manage's integrations page; its prerequisites include working OAuth and completing the App Directory listing steps.
evidence.quote: You've completed the steps to get listed on the App Directory

evidence.claim: An integration that talks to both Clio Manage and Clio Platform needs two separate developer applications.
evidence.quote: you'll currently need to create both a Clio Manage client application and a Clio Platform client application.

evidence.claim: The Manage API changelog has no entry on install caps, unreviewed-app limits or distribution policy; its newest entry is dated 2026-04-08.
evidence.quote: Release Date:** 2026-04-08

evidence.claim: A probe of the Manage authorize endpoint with an invalid client_id produced no OAuth error and redirected to a Clio sign-in page, so the endpoint is live but client_id validation was not visible without signing in.
A third-party integration consultancy says a firm admin must grant the app access per account.
evidence.quote: The firm's admin grants your app access, per account

evidence.claim: A third-party consultancy reports Clio does not offer custom rate increases, consistent with Clio's own docs.
evidence.quote: Clio doesn't offer custom rate increases

evidence.claim: Developers can start with a free 7-day Clio Manage trial; to keep access after the trial they must apply for a free developer account, which Clio reviews and may approve.
evidence.quote: Our team will review the application and, if eligible, your trial account will be converted to a developer account.

evidence.claim: Clio offers no separate sandbox, so the trial or developer account is the test environment; trial signup is per region (US, EU, CA, AU).
evidence.quote: Clio does not have a separate sandbox environment.

evidence.claim: Creating a Manage app for a single firm (private app) requires a paid Clio account to get the app key and secret; apps are unavailable on the EasyStart pricing tier.
evidence.quote: You will need access to a paid Clio account to create apps and get your app key and secret.

evidence.claim: Clio Manage private apps are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be listed in the App Directory, yet each firm user still goes through the OAuth authorization flow.
evidence.quote: Private apps for Clio Manage are not reviewed by Clio and cannot be published in Clio's App Directory.

evidence.claim: The Manage app form requires a name, website URL, at least one redirect URI, access permissions, and acceptance of Clio's Developer Terms of Service; description, icon, support URL and deauthorization callback are optional.
evidence.quote: Developer Terms of Service | true | You must accept the Developer Terms of Service to build an integration with Clio.

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs are declared on the app and each authorize request's redirect_uri must match one of them.
evidence.quote: The URL must match one of the redirect URLs specified in your application settings.

open_questions: Is there an install or user cap for unreviewed or unlisted Manage apps used by many firms? None was found in the docs or the changelog.
Clio publishes no sensitive or restricted permission tiers. Do any permissions trigger extra review?
Clio publishes no end-to-end timeline for an App Directory listing (questionnaire, demo, listing).
The live app form, its exact field labels, any PKCE option and the permission checklist were not inspected because the portal requires login.
Does Composio offer a managed Clio app? It is not in the catalog. Check the Composio dashboard.
Are refresh tokens rotated on refresh? This is not documented.
The content of the Developer Terms of Service and any partner-program fees were not retrieved.
Rejection reasons for an App Directory listing, beyond the security red flags and demo criteria, were not found.
